cards.name: Strike

definition.name: Strike
definition.flavor:
First cut of the hamlets.

Made with whatever edge the hamlet owns. Marl's Hollow sends one climber each winter, chosen at the well, and the chosen spends the last evening at the whetting post learning this and nothing more.

The marked learned a thousand cuts. It did them no good.

cards.name: Defend

definition.name: Defend
definition.flavor:
First guard of the road.

Two crossed lines upon a cairn stone: hold. Cut by climbers for climbers, before the Burning, when the ring was closed to the unmarked.

The mark does not say what to hold against, nor for how long.

cards.name: Footwork

definition.name: Footwork
definition.flavor:
Steps cut into the road.

Too even to be natural, too worn to be recent. The Forsaken credit them to the climbers before. They run past the farthest point any Forsaken is known to have reached, and some lead onto the viaducts, older than the kingdom.

Climbers before you cut steps. Use them.

cards.name: Evasive Guard

definition.name: Evasive Guard
definition.flavor:
Sidestep of the Pale Marches ice-fishers.

The lakes have not thawed since the Burning. The ice cracks all the year round, and gives only beneath a second pair of feet; the fishers learned to trust the sound.

Widow Arne of Sallow Lake says the sound changed last winter. She fishes no longer.

cards.name: Dodge Roll

definition.name: Dodge Roll
definition.flavor:
Tumble of the ship-breakers.

Learned upon hulls that shift with every tide at the Grave of Ships. The hulls were already rotting at anchor when the trade stopped, and on the night of the Burning, every hold went warm at once.

Gull-Bet's gang opened the holds the following spring. She has not said what was inside.

cards.name: Gorefire Slash

definition.name: Gorefire Slash
definition.flavor:
Art of the sellswords of the Bastion.

The hired blades who held the Fell Courtyard wetted their steel with their own blood before each watch, for the Gorefire takes more readily to a blade already red.

The Wardens called it discipline. The sellswords knew it as a price, paid in advance.

cards.name: Crimson Cleave

definition.name: Crimson Cleave
definition.flavor:
Wide cut of the Fell Courtyard watch.

Taught for a gate choked with bodies. On the night the Bastion burned, the dead came up the Muster Stair in numbers the watch had no word for, and this was the only answer it had.

The gate log names the watch whole at the bell. Its hand changes halfway down the page.

cards.name: Shield Bash

definition.name: Shield Bash
definition.flavor:
Rim-strike of the Wardens' shield line.

Drilled in the years of the Spring Wars, when envoys of the Northern Holds came to the Bastion gate to haggle the price of a spring. The Wardens struck with the rim, for the face bore the gilded crest.

Twice the Holds were struck. Twice they paid.

cards.name: Quickstep

definition.name: Quickstep
definition.flavor:
Footwork of the Bastion's hired blades.

After the Burning the weald's spring would not turn, and green came up between the courtyard flags. The sellswords learned short, flat steps upon the moss. The Wardens, who never stood where the footing was worst, did not.

The steps are counted to a dawn peal that brings no dawn.

cards.name: Guard Counter

definition.name: Guard Counter
definition.flavor:
Riposte of the sworn Wardens.

The enemy commits; the Bastion answers, and its answer is always the greater. So the Wardens taught the drill, and so they told of the Spring Wars, in which they claimed never to have struck first.

The Northern Holds remember it otherwise.

cards.name: Iron Resolve

definition.name: Iron Resolve
definition.flavor:
Standing order of the Bastion.

Read at the muster peal: a Warden holds until relieved, and relief comes by the bell. The bell-roll kept the names of all who held.

After the Burning, the roll runs on for many pages, in a hand no scribe knew, bearing names no Warden ever enlisted.

cards.name: Serrated Blade

definition.name: Serrated Blade
definition.flavor:
Saw-backed blade from the forges beneath the Bastion ridge.

Weald smiths filed its teeth for clearing briar, and the Wardens took it up when the Blight came out of the woods. The smiths were never paid for the change of use.

How the briar learned to bleed, the smiths will not speak of.

cards.name: Enter: Gorefire

definition.name: Enter: Gorefire
definition.flavor:
The breaking stance, first of the Wardens' two.

The drill is to hold the flame in the blade, not the hand. Sergeants warned that the stance takes the hand if held too long. Sellswords held it longest of all, which the Wardens took for greed.

Hold the flame in the blade; it still takes the hand.

cards.name: Enter: Bulwark

definition.flavor:
The holding stance, second of the Wardens' two.

Low and square, shield set to the hinge side. The Wardens called the gate a wall a man could carry, and held that no gate kept in this stance had ever fallen.

That teaching was set down before the Burning, and was never amended.

In the illustration, the Knight lies upon his back.

cards.name: Rend

definition.name: Rend
definition.flavor:
Tearing cut for the rot of the weald.

Written into the field-book after the Burning, by whoever keeps it now. It bids the reader cut the rot from hound and hamlet folk alike, for the rot came up the river road with the Court's traders.

cards.name: Twinblade Flurry

definition.flavor:
Two short blades, worked in turn, as the weald's sellswords used them.

Too poor for a shield and too proud to carry a Warden's, they were hired for the Bastion's narrow gates. It is said part of their wage was paid in marks rather than coin: a right to the city's warmth.

Those who refused the mark are the ones who tell of it.

cards.name: Sanguine Pact

definition.name: Sanguine Pact
definition.flavor:
Soldier's bargain of the Bastion's lesser shrine.

Blood spilled from an enemy is sworn to the one who spilled it. The Wardens thought it a harmless field-born custom, like the harvest tithe. The Chapel called it a mockery of the Writing, and fined the shrine.

The fine was paid. The shrine was in use the night of the Burning.

Oath of the Wardens, sworn with the sword hand upon the gate.

Sworn Wardens bore the flame-mark from birth, and the oath was laid over it as a second promise. Sellswords swore it with no first promise beneath, and so the Wardens held them less bound.

What that meant on the night of the Burning, no oath foretold.

cards.name: Stargazer

definition.name: Stargazer
definition.flavor:
The long watch at the eyepiece.

The Astronomer kept it a hundred years by his own count, recording the coal's dimming and never its meaning. The Chapel admired his restraint.

His apprentices believed he watched something he had already resolved not to describe.

definition.name: Astral Armor
definition.flavor:
Mantle of cold light, after Starwatch Terrace.

The terrace upon the Drowned Coast was paved in starstone, that the apprentices might measure the new tower's draw. The paving never warmed, and the salt spray never dried upon it.

A Saint was sent to bless the stones. She asked to be posted elsewhere.

cards.name: Moonrend Cut

definition.name: Moonrend Cut
definition.flavor:
Crescent stroke of the Observatory's night-porters.

The porters walked the Basalt Stair with lanterns and curved blades, and claimed the moon's passage over the caldera showed them where to cut. The Starwatch called it folklore, and employed them regardless.

Their blades are found in the lower galleries, in hands no longer quite their own.

Column of falling light.

Modelled upon a fall the Astronomer charted in advance. He foresaw where it would strike upon the caldera rim, and sent no warning to the mine camps there, for they were unmarked, and absent from the Court's maps.

His margin gives the fall's weight to the grain. Of the camps, nothing.

definition.flavor:
Sorcery of the Starwatch, drawn from the moon-table.

In the last years before the Burning, the Astronomer observed that as the moon waxed, the coal in the Crown dimmed in equal measure. He named it coincidence, and kept the moon-table no longer.

What he would not record, his apprentices remembered.

Communion of the Feral Ember.

The Chapel passed one cup along the pews, that the congregation be one body before the fire. The Feral Ember revived the rite with another cup.

We pass one cup along the pews, and every mouth is red.

Rite of gathering the failing.

Performed in the sick-wards of the crown-born, that the dying need not linger. The Wandering Physician, who served in those wards, kept his own list of those gathered. The ward rolls name none of them.

Many he had expected to recover.

definition.name: Transfusion
definition.flavor:
Communion of blood, between Saint and dying.

Blood poured from cup to cup, for the dying of good family. The rubric speaks of the Saint giving, never receiving. Novice Wen wrote that the flow ran both ways.

The Saints rose from the rite looking younger.

cards.name: Blightward

definition.name: Blightward
definition.flavor:
Cloth laid over an unfinished brand.

Begun for the Herald, whose mark began to burn on the night of the Burning and stopped partway. The Chapel remnant now lays such cloths over the brands of its dead, and teaches that the fire will return to finish its work.

The fire started on me and stopped. I do not know why.

cards.name: Martyr's Blood

definition.name: Martyr's Blood
definition.flavor:
Offering of the Saint's own blood.

Made at the altar when the censer ran low, for a Saint's blood was held to burn hotter than any incense. When the censers were cleaned in the years of the Spire, dried blood lay layered beneath the ash.

We spend ourselves at the altar, and the censer swings faster.

Red flowers upon the graves of the crown-born.

They first appeared in the Furnace Chapel's garden in the Long Winter. The remnant tends them as a sign that the dead are giving yet.

They spread fastest where the earth is freshly turned. The remnant has begun turning more.

cards.name: Thorn Halo

definition.name: Thorn Halo
definition.flavor:
Crown of briar, worn at the feast of the Founding.

In memory of the first Saint, who by Chapel tradition wore thorns in the caldera; each thorn stood for a name carried. In the Long Winter, the Thorn Matriarch grew a crown of her own.

The remnant counts her a Saint. She was a Warden, and never swore to them.

definition.name: Communion
definition.flavor:
Sharing of warmth, as kept at the Tidebound Chapel.

The Saints raised that chapel upon the Drowned Coast to keep watch upon the Spire, which they called heresy. Its congregation shrank with each winter after the Spire was finished.

We watched from Tidebound Chapel and never saw the heresy lit.

definition.flavor:
Oath of the Goldbough crest.

A gilded branch, three flames upon three twigs: the kingdom and its hearths. Novices swore it at their first vigil, before they were told what the hearths were fed.

The crest above the Furnace Chapel's nave bears a fourth twig, bare, blamed upon a careless gilder.

Penitent's walk down the nave.

Scourge in hand, while the congregation answered each blow. The number of blows was set by the number of names written that season. In the last seasons before the Burning, the rite lasted the night.

We walk the nave with the scourge, and the pews answer.

cards.name: Blight Nova

definition.name: Blight Nova
definition.flavor:
Reading of every name, aloud and at once.

Composed by the Furnace Saint after the Burning. The novices say it is what the fire did that night, and that the rite exists so it will be remembered. The remnant holds it holiest of the liturgies.

It has never been performed to its end.

Foreigners, criminals, and in the last years, the bought-marked of whom the Chapel had not been told. The rubric forbids a name upon the headstone, and calls this discretion.

The lower cemetery stands blank by the thousand.

cards.name: Zealotry

definition.name: Zealotry
definition.flavor:
Creed of the Feral Ember.

Each wound is a door the fire walks through. Its priests bless wounds rather than bind them, and hold that the Chapel knew as much, and hid it behind a ledger.

Its converts do not live long. More come each week.

cards.name: Blood Harvest

definition.name: Blood Harvest
definition.flavor:
Reaping of the field of the marked.

So the liturgy names the gathering of names at the close of a plague year. The Saints went out with sickles and ledgers, and the rite is spoken throughout as thanksgiving.

We reap the field of the marked, and give thanks.

The rubric bids the officiant pray louder, and nothing more. The Saints held that the fire heeds the strength of a voice; the novices, that the rubric was written for the family.

We kept the censer swinging when the hearth went dark.

definition.name: Blightward Lash
definition.flavor:
Scourge turned upon one's own rot.

A discipline the Herald took up after the Burning: to cut the Blight from their own flesh and turn it outward. The Chapel remnant condemns it as heresy against the fire's gift.

Twice the remnant has sent a novice to ask how it is done.

definition.flavor:
Warming of a dying hand.

The Chapel's nursing sisters did it with a coal wrapped in cloth, that the fire might find the hand gentle. The Wandering Physician learned it from them, and does it without the coal.

It seems to work as well. He cannot say what working means.

cards.name: Ambush

definition.name: Ambush
definition.flavor:
Opening of the frozen docks.

Strike from beneath a bridge, from behind, before the other has decided there is a fight at all. The docks learned it from the Court's surgeons, who walked the bridges by night with their bags, and always arrived first.

Their day-books record house calls, but no houses.

cards.name: Shiv

definition.name: Shiv
definition.flavor:
Sliver of iron from the rail of the Fourth Bridge.

The ironwork froze brittle the night the Court Flame died. Dock children say the railings were cast from the Court's melted oath-tokens, and so are worth more than any blade in the right hands.

Whose hands are right, the children will not tell.

Knife-work of the Tollmouth fence.

He pays only for quick cuts, holding that a slow cut is a confession and a quick one an accident. Before the Decree, a dock child caught with a knife was hanged, not branded.

The fence considers that the better age.

cards.name: Deathblow

definition.name: Deathblow
definition.flavor:
Killing stroke of the frozen docks.

Struck where the river keeps what the surgeons leave. The river does not thaw, the docks say, because it is full, and the Court built more bridges rather than ask why.

Beneath the ice the Marrow Organist plays the funeral service. He has never reached its end.

definition.flavor:
Whole vial, all at once.

The surgeons measured doses by the drop and wrote each one down. The docks pour the vial and write nothing, which is why the surgeons' ledgers hold so many unexplained recoveries.

The docks' ledgers hold the rest.

definition.name: Prepare
definition.flavor:
Hands warmed before the work.

Cold hands drop knives. Dock children learn to warm their hands before they learn to steal, and never at a fire another has lit. A borrowed fire is a debt, and the docks collect.

The fires on the Citadel side burn more than wood.

An arrow through the hem, not the heart.

Dock archers learned it on the gulls first, then on the Court's bailiffs, whose long coats caught on every piling. A pinned bailiff is a patient one.

The docks still tell which bailiff wore the longest coat, and laugh.

cards.name: Arrow Volley

definition.name: Arrow Volley
definition.flavor:
Loose, nock, loose again.

The dock crews kept a barrel of salvaged arrows beneath every stair, few of them straight. A volley did not need them straight, only many and quick, and the crews were both.

The barrels are empty now. Nobody admits to refilling them.

One arrow, one seam in the armour.

The stitched knights of the Court wear plate sewn at the joints, and the stitching is the weak place. A dock archer who knows a surgeon's work knows where to aim.

Some of them learned it on the surgeons' tables.

The fish on the docks are said to be larger than they were.

Single cut from the scabbard, as it is done beyond the marches.

The curved blades reached the ring in the years of the Mark Trade, borne by foreign lords who paid to be warm there. They burned with the rest of the marked, far from home, and left their swords where they fell.

The merchant knows whose each one was. He sells that separately.

definition.flavor:
Whetstone from the cairn.

At the Grave of the Nameless, the custom is to take one and leave one. The stones are weald sandstone, marches slate, black glass of the reach. One is starstone.

Within the year, someone always carries it back.

Most have been worn thin by more than one wearer.

definition.flavor:
Maps scratched upon cairn stones.

Left by climbers who came back down, or meant to. The hamlet councils copy the true ones and burn the rest, and each winter argue which were which.

The oldest shows a fourth road leading off the ring toward the coast. It has not been burned.

Bastion masons rubbed grit into their forearms until the grit stayed. They said a wall that forgets to be a wall is only a heap, and a mason who forgets is the same.

cards.name: Bastion

definition.name: Bastion
definition.flavor:
Tower shield from the Bastion's walls.

Heavy as a door, nearly as tall. The Wardens set such shields in the embrasures to fight from, never to carry. Climbers carry them regardless, for a moving wall is better than a still one.

The weight bows the bearer forward, as the Wardens once bowed before the Bastion.

definition.flavor:
Shield with nails driven through the boss.

The nails are from the Bastion's own gates. It is said a sellsword made it on the night of the Burning, from the gate he was hired to hold. His name is not known.

No bearer since has drawn the nails.

cards.name: Rime Thrust

definition.flavor:
Frost spear of the Pale Marches.

Its point was reforged from the broken blade of a Court knight, and marches steel keeps its frost long after leaving the cold. The ice-fishers who made it say the knight gave the blade freely, before the Decree, for a winter's fish.

The ice-fishers keep no records.

cards.name: Kiln Cleave

definition.flavor:
Axe of the Dead Foundry.

The Foundry's fires went out with the Crown Flame, and its forges have been warm ever since, though none has lit them. Corran, a foundryman, broke this axe from a cold mould at dawn and carried it up the Basalt Stair.

He says no one poured it.

cards.name: Vesper Ward

definition.flavor:
Ward of the Chapel's evening bell-ringers.

A chime rung at vespers to close the day. Its bell was taken long ago; only the frame and the ward remain. Climbers who carry it say it rings at dusk regardless.

A Chapel ward, rung at vespers. The bell is gone.

cards.name: Blighted Transmute

definition.name: Blighted Transmute
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Stamina. Draw {draw} cards. Pay 12 Ashen Blight. Exhaust.
definition.flavor:
A borrowed breath leaves its name in ash.

The first black veins were mistaken for soot beneath the skin. Those who carried the mark learned that a borrowed breath left a debt after the flame had gone. Some grew stronger while counting it; none found the count growing smaller.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

cards.name: Frost Counter

definition.name: Frost Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a frost Counter: 2 Ward and 1 Poise return.
definition.flavor:
Winter keeps the answering touch.

The Starwatch kept bowls of water beside the lenses through winter. Apprentices learned to read the skin of ice before it cracked. Their notes survived the Burning, folded inside cloth that still stiffens when a stranger touches it.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

cards.name: Fire Counter

definition.name: Fire Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a fire Counter: 2 Ward return.
definition.flavor:
The hearth sends another flame home.

The Bastion's night watch carried coals between the outer posts. A dying ember could reveal a footprint beneath fresh snow, or warn a sleeping guard before the gate gave way. Every watchman learned to keep the smallest flame alive.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

cards.name: Lightning Counter

definition.name: Lightning Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a lightning Counter: 2 Ward return.
definition.flavor:
The returning current remembers every rail.

Storms found the Observatory's iron stairs long before any scholar could name their path. Apprentices marked the scorched rails, then wrapped their hands in dry cloth. The surviving diagrams begin with a warning to watch where the current returns.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

cards.name: Force Counter

definition.name: Force Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a force Counter: 0 Ward and 3 Poise return.
definition.flavor:
A held weight waits for its answer.

At the Basalt Stair, porters steadied heavy crates without touching their broken handles. The Astronomer recorded the trick as a measured displacement. Those who carried the crates remembered only the sudden weight in their wrists when their concentration failed.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

definition.name: Illusion Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a illusion Counter: 1 Ward and 1 Poise return.
definition.flavor:
The second reflection keeps its distance.

The apprentices worked beside darkened lenses until they could distinguish a reflection from its source. One kept a second chair for a companion nobody else remembered. The chair was found warm after the Observatory had stood empty for years.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

definition.name: Divine Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a divine Counter: 2 Ward return.

Pilgrims carried little lamps through the Chapel's long passages, tending each flame before their own food. The rite outlived the voices that taught it. An empty hand held over a stranger's wound still remembers the warmth of that watch.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

definition.name: Decay Counter
definition.textTemplate: Gain {gainBarrier} Barrier. Prepare a decay Counter: 2 Ward return.
definition.flavor:
The bitter garden receives another seed.

Gardeners beneath the Chapel sifted bitter ash through exhausted soil. A root could be fed or strangled by the same handful, depending on the season. Their last ledger names each bed twice, once for its bloom and once for its silence.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

cards.name: Rot Mote

definition.name: Rot Mote
definition.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. May add {crimsonBlight} crimsonBlight buildup; upcasting improves its chance.
definition.flavor:
A bitter seed forgets the season.

Gardeners beneath the Chapel sifted bitter ash through exhausted soil. A root could be fed or strangled by the same handful, depending on the season. Their last ledger names each bed twice, once for its bloom and once for its silence.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

Every road begins with something broken.

cards.name: Crown of Cinders

definition.name: Crown of Cinders
definition.flavor:
Wear the heat for one more blow.

A smith twisted a circlet from furnace wire and set it above his workbench. Apprentices raised it before their final strike, a foolish ceremony that taught them to finish deliberately. The workshop is cold now. The lesson survives in hands blackened by other fires.

Finish while the iron remembers warmth.

definition.flavor:
Cold gives the sky another face.

During the deepest winter, frost covered the Observatory’s polished plates before dawn. The apprentices saw their own hands reflected among unfamiliar stars. They were ordered to scrape the plates clean, but some preserved the patterns on paper, learning a second reading from the cold.

The reflection keeps what warmth forgets.

The scattered points still belong together.

A careful hand finds one more measure.

cards.name: Gravitic Knot

definition.name: Gravitic Knot
definition.flavor:
Draw the loose threads toward one point.

The Observatory’s chart weights hung from cords tied in a common knot. A careless pull could drag an entire night’s readings from the table. The starseers kept the knot as a warning, then learned to read the same gathering pressure in a crowded field of stars.

What gathers closely becomes difficult to move.

Dark glass admits a patient eye.

The darkest lens in the Observatory was stored apart from the others. Students had to sit with it until their eyes adjusted, naming what they could see before reaching for another chart. Those who hurried found only their own reflection, pale and uncertain in the glass.

Wait until the darkness offers a line.

The narrow opening will not remain.

cards.name: Firmament Ward

definition.name: Firmament Ward
definition.flavor:
Set the next light beneath a shelter.

The upper stair once carried covered lanterns so observers could climb without spoiling their night vision. Most covers have rusted shut. A starseer learns from the few that still open: guard the flame before ascending, and the same small light will carry further than expected.

A sheltered spark can outlast the climb.

Let the eye follow the wrong point.

A tailor in the Pale Marches distracted impatient customers with a bright needle while measuring their coats with the other hand. Her apprentice remembered the movement after the shop closed. On colder streets, a harmless flash of steel could make a dangerous hand hesitate.

The smallest motion can delay the largest.

cards.name: Back Alley Cut

definition.name: Back Alley Cut
definition.flavor:
Find the door behind the guard.

The narrow lanes beside the market forced watchmen to carry their shields edgewise. A runner learned which corners made them turn, and which left a gap beside the ribs. The market is abandoned, but its angles still teach anyone willing to walk without a lantern.

The wall protects only the facing side.

cards.name: Silent Exchange

definition.name: Silent Exchange
definition.flavor:
Take a breath, leave a burden.

A smuggler kept two bundles ready whenever the river patrol approached. She opened both, letting the officer choose which to search while the useful parcel changed hands behind his shoulder. The river crossing is gone. The habit of choosing what to relinquish remains surprisingly useful.

Carry the thing that carries you onward.

cards.name: Wire Snare

definition.name: Wire Snare
definition.flavor:
A shaken step finds the waiting thread.

Thin wire once kept scavenging animals out of a merchant’s drying shed. It caught them only after the loose boards beneath their feet gave way. A rogue who studies the ruined frame learns that a trap needs little strength when another mistake has already unbalanced its prey.

Wait for the footing to betray them.

cards.name: Nightstep

definition.name: Nightstep
definition.flavor:
The smoke conceals the waiting blade.

A courier crossed the furnace yards at dusk, using each fresh plume to hide her passage between gates. She never hurried through clear air. The yards have fallen quiet, but the rhythm survives: disappear long enough to place the next step where no one expects it.

Let the edge emerge after the shadow.

cards.name: Carrion Cut

definition.name: Carrion Cut
definition.flavor:
Watch which strength has already gone.

The hunters beyond the Bastion judged a wounded animal by the way it favored the slope. They saved their hardest strokes until the failing leg could no longer turn. A rogue learns the same cruel patience among the dead, where every remaining movement deserves careful attention.

A failing step opens the last path.

cards.name: Twinshade

definition.name: Twinshade
definition.flavor:
Two edges share a single shadow.

A pair of knives was found wrapped in the same strip of black cloth beneath a bridge. Their handles were worn differently, though their edges matched. Whoever carried them had practiced drawing both without a sound, leaving no pause between the first wound and the second.

The answer follows before the question ends.

cards.name: Last Laugh

definition.name: Last Laugh
definition.flavor:
Save your breath until the door is open.

A condemned trickster escaped the Court by greeting the guards politely and falling behind their raised shields. The record notes the embarrassment more carefully than the missing prisoner. Rogues pass the story onward as a lesson: wit buys time, but a guarded retreat makes use of it.

Laugh only when the footsteps are yours.

definition.flavor:
Offer warmth to the hand that remains.

A pilgrim gathered the ashes of a roadside hearth into a little cloth pouch. They carried no heat, but touching the pouch reminded him to tend the living before honoring the dead. Heralds keep the gesture, giving a small kindness room beside the heavier rites.

The living still have a road ahead.

cards.name: Blood Censer

definition.name: Blood Censer
definition.flavor:
The bearer pays before the smoke rises.

A censer from the Furnace Chapel bears a dark groove where its chain rubbed the keeper’s palm. He could have padded the iron, but chose to feel the weight of each procession. Heralds studying the worn link remember that carrying a rite asks something of its bearer.

Keep the weight within the living hand.

Name the wound before it names you.

A chapel manuscript lists the signs of crimson sickness beside the prayers for its victims. Later hands added corrections between the lines, unwilling to mistake comfort for a cure. A herald reads both columns together, learning how a measured voice can make a hidden affliction visible.

What is recognized can no longer hide.

The last bearer must also come home.

Give a little while it is yours to give.

A traveler left a coal at every sheltered hearth along the chapel road. By the final mile, her own brazier was nearly empty. She survived because another traveler had done the same before her. The herald’s lesson is measured generosity, practiced before need becomes desperation.

A small offering can wait for tomorrow.

Keep the measure among the broken names.

The ossuary keeper sang while sorting fragments from ruined memorial stones. Each verse gave him time to read one more name before placing it aside. The work could never be finished, but its rhythm kept his hands moving when grief threatened to stop them altogether.

There is another verse while breath remains.

tags.label: Card
tags.blurb: What a card IS — its school, form and feel. Carried by cards, by the classes that lean on them, and by the equipment that rewrites them.

tags.label: Creature
tags.blurb: What a creature IS. Gates proc resistance, and the one domain the engine reads at runtime.

tags.label: Item
tags.blurb: What a piece of gear DOES beyond its numbers, and what a run pickup is.

tags.label: Run
tags.blurb: Run structure — what an event, an encounter or an unlock is about.

tags.label: Item type
tags.blurb: What a piece of equipment IS, as the Armoury and the smith name it. Distinct from the card domain: a Blade item type and a Blade card school are different facts about the same sword.

tags.label: Grant source
tags.blurb: Where a starting card came from. The composed deck deals bound cards in this vocabulary's authored order, so adding a source is a row here rather than a code change. Nothing WEARS these — the `grant` family exists to declare them, the way `effect` declares which words a damage effect may carry.

tags.label: Combat presentation
tags.blurb: Sprite selection only; never damage or resistance identity.

tags.label: Attack source
tags.blurb: Source profile supplying an attack; separate from damage type.

tags.label: Delivery
tags.blurb: How a direct attack reaches its targets.

tags.label: Damage type
tags.blurb: Identity of a typed HP damage component.

tags.label: Technique
tags.blurb: Conditions for explicit technique bonuses.

tags.label: Theme
tags.blurb: Build synergies; tags alone grant no effects.

tags.label: Property
tags.blurb: What a holder CONFERS while it is held. Each property node has exactly one entry in nodeEffects.json; the holder grants it, and it leaves when the holder does. EVERY family may carry one — what the mount path can hold (worn, owned, chosen) is the engine's narrower list, engine/properties.js MOUNTABLE_KINDS.

tags.label: Blade
tags.blurb: Steel and edge — direct weapon work.

tags.label: Bow
tags.blurb: A bow draw and arrow release.

tags.label: Guard
tags.blurb: Bracing, blocking, holding the line.

tags.label: Blood
tags.blurb: Bleed, and the letting of it.

tags.label: Gorefire
tags.blurb: The blood-and-flame stance.

tags.label: Starstone
tags.blurb: Astral sorcery — charges and combos.

tags.label: Ritual

tags.label: Searing Edge
tags.blurb: A direct hit carries an authored Bleed buildup rider; the tag supplies no extra damage by itself.

tags.label: Guarded Strike
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player currently has positive Block before an attack resolves.

tags.label: Bloodstep
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy has positive Bleed buildup before the card resolves.

tags.label: Hammerfall
tags.blurb: Marks an attack with an explicit Break-damage rider; HP damage and Break damage remain separate values.

tags.label: Forgewake
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player has already played a Guard card during this turn.

tags.label: Crimson Reprisal
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player lost HP since their previous turn began; paying HP counts, losing Block does not.

tags.label: Last Stand
tags.blurb: Tests whether current HP is at or below 50% of current maximum HP before resolution.

tags.label: War Tempo
tags.blurb: Tests whether at least two Heavy cards have already been played by the acting player during this turn.

tags.label: Wide Cleave
tags.blurb: Marks one authored attack effect that independently hits every living enemy; it is not a separate hit per tag.

tags.label: Ember Crown
tags.blurb: Marks a one-charge bonus to the next direct attack this turn; the charge expires at turn end and cannot stack with itself.

tags.label: Dreadweight
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy is currently Staggered before a direct hit.

tags.label: Oathscar
tags.blurb: Identifies the first Guard card after the acting player has lost HP since their previous turn began; at most once per turn.

tags.label: Wound Harvest
tags.blurb: Identifies a credited kill of an enemy that had positive Bleed buildup immediately before the killing hit.

tags.label: Cinder Orbit
tags.blurb: Tests whether the immediately preceding card played this turn by the same player was a spell.

tags.label: Lunar Guard
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player has already spent at least 2 Mana this turn; refunded Mana does not erase spending.

tags.label: Comet Mark
tags.blurb: Marks an attack that applies an authored Vulnerable rider after its direct damage.

tags.label: Rime Mirror
tags.blurb: Marks a defensive spell with an authored Frost buildup rider against one selected enemy.

tags.label: Constellation
tags.blurb: Tests how many distinct Starstone card IDs the acting player has played this turn; two copies of one ID count once.

tags.label: Mana Weave
tags.blurb: Marks an authored Mana restoration rider, capped at one activation per owning player per turn.

tags.label: Gravity Snare
tags.blurb: Marks a spell with an authored Weak rider after its direct damage.

tags.label: Nightglass
tags.blurb: Marks a one-charge direct-spell-damage bonus to the next spell this turn; no stacking and no carry into the next turn.

tags.label: Eclipse Window
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy has positive Frost buildup or is Frost-exposed before resolution.

tags.label: Warded Casting
tags.blurb: Marks a one-charge Mana discount for the next spell this turn; cost cannot fall below zero and the charge expires at turn end.

tags.label: Celestial Echo
tags.blurb: Identifies the second play of the same Starstone card ID in a turn; the condition can activate once per turn.

tags.label: Cold Memory
tags.blurb: Marks an authored amount of Block retained into the next turn; retention sources use the largest allowance, not their sum.

tags.label: Astral Convergence
tags.blurb: Identifies the third distinct Starstone card ID played by the same player in a turn; once per turn.

tags.label: Ash Opener
tags.blurb: Tests whether this is the acting player's first card played this turn.

tags.label: Discard Weave
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player has discarded a card this turn; Exhaust and a spent card entering discard do not count.

tags.label: Crooked Guard
tags.blurb: Marks a direct attack with an authored Weak rider; the rider resolves after damage.

tags.label: Exposed Flank
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy has exactly zero Block immediately before the hit.

tags.label: Sleight of Hand
tags.blurb: Marks an authored draw-then-discard sequence; the player chooses the discarded card and ordinary hand limits apply.

tags.label: Tether Cut
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy currently has Weak or Vulnerable before damage resolves.

tags.label: Smoke Edge
tags.blurb: Marks a one-charge bonus to the next Blade attack this turn; the charge expires at turn end and cannot stack with itself.

tags.label: Carrion Finish
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy is at or below 50% maximum HP before the attack.

tags.label: Paired Strikes
tags.blurb: Marks an attack with exactly two authored direct hits; rank bonuses are divided across the hits.

tags.label: Trapdoor
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player has already played at least one Guile card and one Guard card this turn.

tags.label: Clean Escape
tags.blurb: Identifies the first Guard card played before any attack this turn; once per turn.

tags.label: Razor Debt
tags.blurb: Identifies the first Blade attack after an explicit discard this turn; once per turn.

tags.label: Mercy in Ash
tags.blurb: Marks a defensive card with an authored healing rider; healing cannot exceed maximum HP.

tags.label: Blood Censer
tags.blurb: Marks a card with an explicit HP offering paid before its benefits; the offering cannot reduce HP below 1.

tags.label: Blight Seed
tags.blurb: Marks a direct hit with an authored Crimson Blight buildup rider; this is not Poison.

tags.label: Funeral Guard
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player has HP at or below 50% maximum HP before a Guard card resolves.

tags.label: Ember Tithe
tags.blurb: Marks an explicit, nonlethal HP offering that buys an authored regenerative benefit.

tags.label: Bone Chorus
tags.blurb: Tests whether at least one living enemy has positive Crimson Blight buildup before resolution.

tags.label: Requiem Brand
tags.blurb: Tests whether the selected enemy has positive Crimson Blight buildup before the hit.

tags.label: Pilgrim Shelter
tags.blurb: Tests whether the acting player began this turn at or below 50% maximum HP; later healing does not change that turn's result.

tags.label: Scarred Rite

tags.label: Attack
tags.blurb: Fast strike. Gains extra Poise pressure against a prepared Smash or casting enemy.

tags.label: Defend
tags.blurb: Prepare defense. Physical cards protect Guard; defensive spell cards protect Ward. Smash breaks physical Guard.

tags.label: Counter
tags.blurb: Prepare one reaction. Reduce damage from one eligible hit. A fully absorbed eligible hit triggers a stronger reply; Sweep, Force and Piercing bypass melee Counter.

tags.label: Sweep
tags.blurb: Windmill strike. Bypasses melee Counter; physical Guard and ranged attacks answer it.

tags.label: Ranged
tags.blurb: Ranged delivery avoids melee replies. Ranged Counter, spell Counter and defensive Alteration answer it.

tags.label: Smash
tags.blurb: Heavy strike. Deals extra damage against physical Guard and extra Poise damage when Guard breaks. Fast Attack and Counter answer it.

tags.label: Frost
tags.blurb: Cold control: Frost buildup rewards follow-up attacks and constrains enemy tempo.

tags.label: Fire
tags.blurb: Fire pressure: Burn buildup keeps pressure between turns.

tags.label: Lightning

tags.label: Force

tags.label: Alteration
tags.blurb: Defensive and shaping magic: Ward, resource shaping and control. Answers ranged pressure.

tags.label: Illusion

tags.label: Melee counter
tags.blurb: Replies to eligible melee Attack or Smash. Sweep, Force, Piercing and Ranged bypass this reaction.

tags.label: Ranged counter
tags.blurb: Replies only to incoming physical projectiles. Spells and melee moves do not trigger it.

tags.label: Spell counter
tags.blurb: Intercepts incoming physical ranged moves or spells. Against physical ranged moves, strips Ward without Health retaliation. Against spellcasters, can retaliate against Health.

tagDomains.blurb: Run structure — what an event, an encounter or an unlock is about.

tagDomains.label: Item type
tagDomains.blurb: What a piece of equipment IS, as the Armoury and the smith name it. Distinct from the card domain: a Blade item type and a Blade card school are different facts about the same sword.

tagDomains.label: Grant source
tagDomains.blurb: Where a starting card came from. The composed deck deals bound cards in this vocabulary's authored order, so adding a source is a row here rather than a code change. Nothing WEARS these — the `grant` family exists to declare them, the way `effect` declares which words a damage effect may carry.

tagDomains.label: Combat presentation
tagDomains.blurb: Sprite selection only; never damage or resistance identity.

tagDomains.label: Attack source
tagDomains.blurb: Source profile supplying an attack; separate from damage type.

tagDomains.label: Delivery
tagDomains.blurb: How a direct attack reaches its targets.

tagDomains.label: Damage type
tagDomains.blurb: Identity of a typed HP damage component.

tagDomains.label: Theme
tagDomains.blurb: Build synergies; tags alone grant no effects.

tagDomains.label: Property
tagDomains.blurb: What a holder CONFERS while it is held. Each property node has exactly one entry in nodeEffects.json; the holder grants it, and it leaves when the holder does. EVERY family may carry one — what the mount path can hold (worn, owned, chosen) is the engine's narrower list, engine/properties.js MOUNTABLE_KINDS.

tagDomains.label: Combat camp
tagDomains.blurb: Authored combat identity shared by cards and enemy moves.

tagDomains.label: Combat maneuver
tagDomains.blurb: Authored combat identity shared by cards and enemy moves.

tagDomains.label: Magic school
tagDomains.blurb: Authored combat identity shared by cards and enemy moves.

tagDomains.label: Counter reach
tagDomains.blurb: Authored combat identity shared by cards and enemy moves.

tagFamilies.label: Card
tagFamilies.blurb: Every playable card.

tagFamilies.label: Class
tagFamilies.blurb: A class's identity in card terms — what it leans toward.

tagFamilies.label: Relic
tagFamilies.blurb: Permanent run pickups.

tagFamilies.label: Flask
tagFamilies.blurb: Consumables, refilled at Grace.

tagFamilies.label: Keepsake
tagFamilies.blurb: The boon you start the run holding.

tagFamilies.label: Event
tagFamilies.blurb: Unknown-node encounters.

tagFamilies.label: Encounter
tagFamilies.blurb: Authored fights.

tagFamilies.label: Enemy
tagFamilies.blurb: Creature identity; gates proc resistance at runtime.

tagFamilies.label: Armament
tagFamilies.blurb: Weapons, shields and staves.

tagFamilies.label: Armour
tagFamilies.blurb: Armour sets. Ids repeat per class, so classId is part of the key.

tagFamilies.label: Card profile
tagFamilies.blurb: Equipment-bound core card profiles.

tagFamilies.label: Slot
tagFamilies.blurb: What you can wear, and when you may swap.

tagFamilies.label: Starting kit
tagFamilies.blurb: A class's listed opening loadout.

tagFamilies.label: Unlock
tagFamilies.blurb: What a run can earn.

tagFamilies.label: Effect
tagFamilies.blurb: Damage effects carry card tags; a hit inherits the card's identity.

tagFamilies.label: Grant
tagFamilies.blurb: Where a starting card comes from. No collection: like `effect`, this family exists only to declare a vocabulary — the order bound cards are dealt in.

tagFamilies.label: Location
tagFamilies.blurb: Where a run stops: a classic node type (shrine), the Unknown node's camp, an atlas rest service's type (inn, chapel) or one atlas node by id. No collection — the ids are the map's, checked by model/locations.js. Mounted from arrival to departure (engine/locations.js).

tagFamilies.label: Companion
tagFamilies.blurb: A temporary ally bought at the market (SPEC §14.3). It travels with the run for a number of fights, and what it does is its property rows here, mounted at combat start (engine/properties.js).

tagFamilies.label: Sigil
tagFamilies.blurb: A sigil set into an armament's slot at the blacksmith (SPEC §14.3, §14.4). What it does is its property row here, mounted while its armament is equipped (engine/properties.js).

tagFamilies.label: Class feat
tagFamilies.blurb: A selected class feat confers mounted property rules.

tagFamilies.label: Enemy move
tagFamilies.blurb: An authored enemy action; id is scoped by enemyId.

statuses.name: Strength
statuses.tooltip: Attacks deal +1 damage per stack.

statuses.name: Dexterity
statuses.tooltip: Cards grant +1 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Weak
statuses.tooltip: Deals 25% less attack damage. 1 stack expires each turn.

statuses.name: Vulnerable
statuses.tooltip: Takes 50% more attack damage. 1 stack expires each turn.

statuses.name: Frail
statuses.tooltip: Gains 25% less Block from cards. 1 stack expires each turn.

statuses.name: Bleed
statuses.tooltip: Build-up: points do not decay. At {proc.threshold}, burst for {proc.burstPercent}% of max HP (min {proc.burstMin}, max {proc.burstMax}), ignoring Block, plus {proc.poiseDamage} Poise damage — then the build-up resets to zero. Fleshy targets briefly resist further Bleed after a burst.

statuses.name: Frost
statuses.tooltip: Build-up: points do not decay. At {proc.threshold}, burst for {proc.burstPercent}% of max HP (min {proc.burstMin}, max {proc.burstMax}), ignoring Block, and the target is left Weak and Frost-Exposed — then the build-up resets to zero.

statuses.name: Insanity
statuses.tooltip: Build-up: points do not decay. At {proc.threshold}, burst for {proc.burstPercent}% of max HP (min {proc.burstMin}, max {proc.burstMax}), ignoring Block, with {proc.poiseDamage} Poise damage and a guaranteed Stagger — then the build-up resets to zero.

statuses.name: Clotted
statuses.tooltip: Just burst — hardened against Bleed: incoming build-up reduced {resists.percent}% for {decay.duration} turns.

statuses.name: Weathered
statuses.tooltip: Just burst — hardened against Frost: incoming build-up reduced {resists.percent}% for {decay.duration} turns.

statuses.name: Resolute
statuses.tooltip: Just burst — hardened against Insanity: incoming build-up reduced {resists.percent}% for {decay.duration} turns.

statuses.name: Frost-Exposed
statuses.tooltip: Takes {tv.pct}% more damage from starstone attacks. Stacks with Vulnerable. {decay.duration} turns.

statuses.name: Unraveled
statuses.tooltip: Takes {tv.pct}% more damage from ritual and blight attacks. Stacks with Vulnerable. {decay.duration} turns.

statuses.name: Crimson Blight
statuses.tooltip: At the start of its turn, loses HP equal to Blight stacks (ignores Block). Stacks do not tick down; the Blight expires entirely after 3 turns. Re-applying adds stacks and refreshes the duration.

statuses.name: Necrotic Blight
statuses.tooltip: At the start of its turn, loses HP equal to Necrotic Blight stacks (ignores Block). Applied by Necrotic damage. Stacks do not tick down and it lasts the whole fight; only a cleanse removes it.

statuses.name: Burn
statuses.tooltip: At the start of its turn, loses HP equal to Burn stacks (ignores Block). One stack burns out each turn.

statuses.name: Regen
statuses.tooltip: At the start of its turn, heals HP equal to Regen stacks. Lasts the whole fight.

statuses.name: Madness
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn: lose 2 HP per stack, gain 1 Energy per stack, then Madness clears.

statuses.name: Staggered
statuses.tooltip: Poise broken: skips its next turn and takes 50% more attack damage until the end of your next turn.

statuses.name: Rallying Standard
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn: gain 1 Strength and take 1 damage (per stack).

statuses.name: Rallying Standard+
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn: gain 1 Strength (per stack).

statuses.name: Unbreakable
statuses.tooltip: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. Block is capped at 30.

statuses.name: Unbreakable+
statuses.tooltip: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. Block is capped at 40.

statuses.name: Goreblood
statuses.tooltip: Poise thresholds no longer increase after filling.

statuses.name: Sanguine Pact
statuses.tooltip: Whenever Bleed bursts on an enemy, gain 2 Strength per stack.

statuses.name: Starstone Charge
statuses.tooltip: A spell was cast this turn: your next Starstone bonus is live. Fades at end of turn.

statuses.name: Stargazer
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn, gain Starstone Charge.

statuses.name: Astral Armor
statuses.tooltip: At the end of your turn, gain 4 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Constellation
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you gain Starstone Charge, deal 4 damage per stack to a random enemy.

statuses.name: Azure Coil
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you play a Skill, gain 2 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Waxing Moon
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn, apply 2 Vulnerable to ALL enemies per stack.

statuses.name: Moonlit Shield
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you gain Starstone Charge, gain 3 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Astromancer
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn, gain Starstone Charge and draw a card.

statuses.name: Thorn Halo
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn, apply 1 Crimson Blight per stack to ALL enemies.

statuses.name: Communion
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your turn, heal 3 HP per stack.

statuses.name: Life Tithe
statuses.tooltip: Whenever an enemy dies, heal 8 HP per stack.

statuses.name: Stigmata
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you lose HP, heal 2 HP per stack.

statuses.name: Zealotry
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you lose HP, deal 3 damage to a random enemy per stack.

statuses.name: Ember Tide
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you heal, gain 1 Strength per stack.

statuses.name: Harbinger of Blight
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you apply Blight (Crimson or Necrotic) to an enemy, heal 1 HP per stack.

statuses.name: Blood Unction
statuses.tooltip: Your attacks apply 2 extra Bleed per hit this turn.

statuses.name: Iron Vow
statuses.tooltip: Whenever you lose HP, gain 3 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Shieldwall Echo
statuses.tooltip: At the start of your next turn: gain 4 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Prepared
statuses.tooltip: Your next setup payoff is empowered. Expires at turn end.

statuses.name: Venom
statuses.tooltip: At turn start, lose HP equal to Venom. 1 stack expires each turn.

statuses.name: Afterimage
statuses.tooltip: Every third card played each combat grants 3 Block per stack.

statuses.name: Deadly Tempo
statuses.tooltip: At turn start, become Prepared and draw 1 card per stack.

statuses.name: Opportunist
statuses.tooltip: When an enemy staggers, become Prepared and draw 1 card per stack.

statuses.name: Envenom
statuses.tooltip: Your attacks apply 1 Venom per stack.

statuses.name: Glass Cannon
statuses.tooltip: Deal 25% more attack damage, and take 25% more.

statuses.name: Magic Vulnerable
statuses.tooltip: Magic-school HP damage is increased while this lasts.

statuses.name: Stance Shifted
statuses.tooltip: You have entered a stance this fight: Oath cards no longer grant Block.

statuses.name: Silenced
statuses.tooltip: Spells cost 1 more Stamina per stack. Immune to Force: each Force hit or effect is stopped and removes 1 stack.

statuses.name: Stoneskin
statuses.tooltip: Your Block is not removed at the start of your next turn.

statuses.name: Bleeding
statuses.tooltip: Lose 1 HP per stack at turn start. Bodily Chance Recovery.

statuses.name: Frozen
statuses.tooltip: One stack denies one Action. Fire thaws; Blunt shatters. Elemental Chance Recovery.

statuses.name: Chilled
statuses.tooltip: The next connected Blunt action deals 25% more damage. Fire thaws.

statuses.name: Sleep
statuses.tooltip: Locks ordinary cards, Counter and card Evade. Rest restores up to 6 HP and 1 Ward per combat. +10% direct damage received per active stack. Break Sleep: 2 SP per stack.

statuses.name: Paralysis
statuses.tooltip: Locks ordinary cards, Counter and card Evade. Break Paralysis: 3 SP per stack. Grounding clears its pressure.

statuses.name: Dazed
statuses.tooltip: Locks ordinary cards, Counter and card Evade. Clear Dazed: 1 SP per stack.

statuses.name: Off Balance
statuses.tooltip: Disadvantage on bodily recovery. One stack expires at turn end.

statuses.name: Prone
statuses.tooltip: +25% Contact damage, −25% Single Near/Far damage. +2/+4 Evade against Near/Far Martial weapons. Stand Up: 1 SP after hand locks clear.

statuses.name: Grounded
statuses.tooltip: Prevents electrical conductivity and backlash; grants Advantage on Paralysis recovery.

statuses.name: Invulnerability
statuses.tooltip: Consume one stack to avoid the next direct damaging action, including all its hits. Status buildup still applies; no Counter return. Damage over time does not consume it.

statuses.name: Decoy
statuses.tooltip: Consume one stack to avoid a Single Near/Far damaging action. Status buildup still applies. Sweep and Holy revelation clear it.

statuses.name: Concealed
statuses.tooltip: Concealment. Sweep and Holy revelation clear it.

statuses.name: Confused
statuses.tooltip: Deals 10% less damage. At the start of its turn, 50% chance to take 3 Poise damage per stack. 1 stack expires each turn.

statuses.name: Slowed
statuses.tooltip: Deals 10% less damage and gains 25% less Block. 1 stack expires each turn.

statuses.name: Entombed
statuses.tooltip: Skips its next turn. Takes 25% less damage while entombed.

stances.name: Gorefire Stance
stances.tooltip: Your attacks apply 2 Bleed per hit. On entering: take 2 damage (ignores Block).

stances.name: Bulwark Stance
stances.tooltip: Whenever you play a Skill, gain 2 Block. On entering: gain 3 Block.

stances.name: Brace
stances.tooltip: Damage taken −25%. On entering: gain 4 Block. On leaving: gain 1 Strength.
